title: Model Methods & Meta Options
description: Add custom behavior to your models and control database structure with Meta class.

slides.title: Custom Model Methods 🛠️
slides.content:
You can define methods on your model classes to add custom logic. Common uses:
- `__str__()`: returns a human‑readable representation
- `get_absolute_url()`: returns the canonical URL for the object
- Any helper method (e.g., `is_recent()`)

These methods can be called in templates or views.

slides.title: Adding Methods

quizData.question: What is the purpose of the `__str__` method in a Django model?

options.text: To define the database table name
To return a string representation of the object, used in admin and shell

quizData.explanation: `__str__` is a Python special method that returns a readable string. In Django, it's used in the admin interface, shell, and templates when you print an object.

slides.title: Meta Class – Model Metadata 📋
slides.content:
Inside a model, you can define a `class Meta` to set various options:

- **`db_table`** – custom database table name (default is `appname_modelname`)
- **`ordering`** – default ordering for queries
- **`verbose_name`** / **`verbose_name_plural`** – human‑readable names
- **`unique_together`** – enforce uniqueness across multiple fields
- **`indexes`** – add database indexes

slides.title: Using Meta Options
slides.content:
class Post(models.Model):
    title = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

    class Meta:
        ordering = ['-created_at']  # newest first
        verbose_name_plural = "Blog Posts"
        db_table = "blog_article"  # custom table name

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use `ordering` to set a sensible default

Setting `ordering` in `Meta` means you don't have to add `.order_by()` every time you query. But be aware it adds overhead to every query – use it when it makes sense for the model.
